name: Ransomware
description: Ransomware encryption event — lateral movement, potential double-extortion leak site.
initialKeyQuestions: What was the initial access vector?
When did encryption begin, and which hosts and shares were affected?
What ransom note or attacker-left IOC was found?
How did the attacker achieve lateral movement or privilege escalation?
Are backups intact and isolated from the network?

initialNextSteps.action: Isolate all affected hosts from the network immediately
initialNextSteps.rationale: Prevent further encryption and lateral movement while preserving evidence
initialNextSteps.pointer: Network switch ports or EDR isolation console

initialNextSteps.action: Preserve volatile memory (RAM dump) of patient zero before any remediation
initialNextSteps.rationale: Memory may contain encryption keys, injected attacker tools, and credentials

initialNextSteps.action: Collect Windows event logs (Security, System, Sysmon) from all affected hosts
initialNextSteps.rationale: Identify initial access, lateral movement, and the encryption process chain

initialNextSteps.action: Check for data exfiltration indicators: large outbound transfers, rclone, MEGAsync
initialNextSteps.rationale: Ransomware groups commonly exfiltrate before encrypting — determines notification obligations
initialNextSteps.pointer: Zeek/Suricata logs, proxy logs, DLP alerts

reportFraming.summaryPrompt: Summarize the ransomware impact, scope, and notification obligations for the board and insurer.

synthesisHint: This is a ransomware case — prioritize T1486 Data Encrypted for Impact, T1490 Inhibit System Recovery (VSS deletion), T1021 Remote Services / lateral movement, and T1567 Exfiltration to Cloud Service (double extortion).
